limits.limit: Review uses explicit bounded sought frames and every-turn four-second overview, with native targeted transitions. No continuous real-time playback or sub-frame timing was measured. Requested source seeks are approximate timestamps; actual decoded presentation timestamps are unset.

Opponent hand names, normal draw identities and search results are hidden. Counted backs are direct fan observations, not identities. No complete discard pile was opened; top cards and recorded plays cannot establish an exhaustive pile.

Poké Ball normal draw is identifiable in animation but is played before a clear unzoomed six-card fan. Five retained cards plus this named draw establish composition and count; sixth fan position is not claimed from a clear view.

First voluntary move follows the draw within about one second. Required +1/+3/+6 captures therefore include played or zoomed hands. Earlier native pre-move frames are separately selected. The grid alone is not start-hand evidence.
Empty-deck notice appears; there is no successful normal draw and no draw-animation-end timestamp. Captures are instead tied to the visible turn-start notice. No card identity is fabricated.

Network waiting message and Lucky Ice Pop coin remain on screen approximately 584-644s. No unrecorded action is reconstructed. Turn ends after waiting without a visible attack; intent to decline attack or manually End Turn is unknown.

First Professor’s Research is established by its visible discard top at 61-67s and two back-only draw animations early in turn 1. Exact click time and opponent draw identities are unknown. Lucky Ice Pop coin face/return on turn 15 is not securely established; turn 17 ends with it visible on the discard top.

board_after is the resolved post-checkup state before the next draw, rather than the attack impact alone. Printed effects and action events separately preserve transient Burn, Sleep and healing. Exact first-turn opponent generated Energy availability is visibly empty.

Live log has the exact 20 slots and printed set identifiers. Filmed QR matches semantic identities and Water Energy. In-game artwork differs for some copies; set/artwork variants are not inferred from QR and no unshown opponent deck slots are guessed.
